tldr: For selecting the best of \(M\) supplied memoryless policies from one stationary behavior trajectory, the bounded-reward finite-POMDP baseline without a uniform stationary occupancy-ratio certificate is \(Q_T^{\mathrm{HW}}(M;t_0,\zeta)\asymp\min\{1,(\log(M)/T)^{1/(2+t_0\zeta)}\}\). One observable common-window median-of-blocks PHIW selector attains this law with its history depth tuned at the universal total-variation envelope one, and the lower bound follows from a common-kernel \(M\)-ary converse on the fixed \(C=2\) subclass. When a radius \(C\) is certified, the sharper law remains \(Q_T(M;t_0,\zeta,C)\asymp\min\{1,\sqrt{\log(M)/T}+((C-1)/C)^{1-\beta}(\log(M)/T)^{\beta/2}\}\). Accepted-bank stat_pomdp_latent_overlap_minimax_v1 already gives the corresponding one-policy stationary-overlap surface and its \(C=1\) and shrinking-overlap boundaries; the contribution here is the supplied-list simple-regret extension, its simultaneous selector, and its common-kernel \(M\)-ary lower experiment. The proved sparse-context finite-word theorem supplies the required likelihood control for stationary prefixes at every depth and list size.
gap: Pointwise POMDP policy evaluation has a matched hidden-memory rate, and offline policy selection is generically no easier than evaluation, but neither result determines the decision loss from comparing \(M\) supplied stationary targets on one dependent, partially observed log. Existing multiple-policy evaluation theory uses a sampling oracle and fully observed finite-horizon states.
fill: The project couples arbitrary-start blockwise PHIW control with a sparse exceptional-context code. The former converts pointwise bias and variance into an observable expected-regret selector without a \(\log T\) loss. The latter preserves the target value gap and the exact logged survival exponent under one behavior law. Proving the contextual observed-word KL inequality completes the matched frontier and its overlap/list-size phase transition.
